result.title: Color wave: A systematic evaluation of active screen illumination for injection attack detection in remote face authentication
result.summary: Remote face authentication requires protection against both presentation attacks and biometric data injection attacks prior to face matching. Methods based on active screen illumination appear promising for both by introducing randomized visual stimuli through the user's device screen and evaluating the corresponding facial responses. Although such methods have been more studied for presentation attack detection (PAD), their systematic evaluation for injection attack detection (IAD) remains limited. To address this gap, we first classify injected content into static images, prerecorded videos, and real-time deepfakes based on their expected responses to the challenge. We then adapt an active screen-illumination approach into an implementation we term color wave and develop a systematic, injection-specific evaluation protocol. The protocol examines detection effectiveness, generalization across operating conditions, robustness to signal degradation, and susceptibility to selected evasion strategies. The findings demonstrate a strong discriminative signal under controlled conditions but also reveal performance limitations under overexposure, low screen brightness, and subject motion, as well as vulnerabilities to selected evasion strategies. By relating detection outcomes to attack types and operating conditions, this study provides an interpretable assessment of when and why active screen illumination succeeds or fails as an IAD mechanism.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文系统评估「color wave」主动屏幕光照方案在远程人脸认证中检测注入攻击的效果，并按静态图像、预录视频和实时 deepfake 分类考察泛化性、信号退化鲁棒性与规避风险。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究属于生物特征安全与注入攻击检测，虽用屏幕刺激诱发人脸响应，但不涉及 VLM 内部表示、latent 推理状态、证据筛选或停止决策，未发现可供 LVR 借鉴的具体方法线索。
